{{Short description|American research mathematician}}'''Eugene P. Northrop''' (1908–1969) was an American research [[mathematician]] and a math popularizer.

Northrop received his PhD from Yale University in 1934 with thesis advisor [[Einar Hille]]. Northrop held the [[William Rainey Harper]] Chair of [[Mathematics]] at the [[University of Chicago]],<ref>[http://photoarchive.lib.uchicago.edu/db.xqy?one=apf1-01225.xml University of Chicago Archives.]</ref> and frequently served in administrative roles and on technical commissions.<ref>S E Fienberg et al (2012) ''A Statistical Model: Frederick Mosteller’s Contributions to Statistics, Science, and Public Policy'', Springer.</ref> He is most remembered for his 1944 book ''Riddles in Mathematics'',<ref>EP Northrop (1944) ''Riddles in Mathematics: A Book of Paradoxes'', Van Nostrand.</ref> which was well-received by the mathematical community<ref>[[Ernest Nagel|E. Nagel]] (1945) Review of ''Riddles in Mathematics'', ''Journal of Symbolic Logic'' '''10'''(1), 21. {{doi|10.2307/2267205}}</ref> and remains in print as a [[Dover Publications|Dover]] book (first published in 2014).<ref name="Northrop2014">{{cite book|author=Northrop, Eugene P.|title=Riddles in Mathematics: A Book of Paradoxes|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HST0AwAAQBAJ|date=10 June 2014|publisher=Courier Corporation|isbn=978-0-486-79500-3}}</ref>
